summary: Cecil Rhodes built the De Beers diamond monopoly in southern Africa, conquered the lands named Rhodesia with a private army, and as Cape Colony prime minister laid legal groundwork for apartheid.

evidence.note: born July 1853 in Bishop's Stortford, Hertfordshire
dies in 1902 at 49, as the Second Boer War ends
1871 Kimberley diamond find; Rhodes heads there, start of main span
returns to England, splits years between Oxford and the mines
BSAC police and settlers sent into Mashonaland, present-day Zimbabwe
De Beers pass laws, strip searches, compounds and unequal pay for black miners
Matabele war battles: machine guns against African armies
Glen Grey Act: tiny plots, labour tax, disenfranchisement; framed as root of apartheid
Jameson Raid on the Transvaal fails and ends his premiership
long reading of his white-supremacist Confession of Faith
legacy: diamond cartel, Sierra Leone and Congo conflict diamonds to the present

notes: Blood-diamond legacy (Sierra Leone, Second Congo War) and a 2016 conservative defense get a few minutes at the end; treated as legacy via reaches_present, not covered years or setting (SL, CD omitted). Matabele war and Boer War camp deaths are described briefly; mass-atrocity not added. Northern Rhodesia (ZM) only mentioned in passing.
